info.title: Sluby API
info.description:
REST API and delivery gateway for Sluby, decentralized video streaming on the Sia network. Programmatic access uses a scoped API key sent as a `Bearer` token; the Studio UI uses a session cookie.

Every resource belongs to the account (`creator_address`) of the key that made it, and a by-id request for another account’s resource answers 404, as for one that does not exist. A key with the all-zero platform address acts across accounts. Deployment-wide operations data is for that key and for operators, the accounts listed in OPERATOR_USERS and their keys, who see the deployment but still only their own account’s resources.

Errors are JSON `{ "error": "...", "details": [...] }`; `details` lists the invalid fields of a 400. Every response of a key-checked operation carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; over the limit the answer is 429 with `Retry-After`. A path no route serves answers 404 whether or not a key is sent.

bearerAuth.description: A Sluby API key (`sluby_...`) sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys carry scopes: `upload`, `read`, `manage`.

cookieAuth.name: sluby_session
cookieAuth.description: Signed session cookie issued to the Studio after GitHub login.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: Keyset pagination cursor. Pass the `next_cursor` from the previous page to fetch the next one. A cursor that does not decode is a 400.

page.name: page
page.description: Offset page number (alternative to `cursor`; sending both is a 400).

RetryAfter.description: Seconds until the rate-limit window resets.

RateLimitLimit.description: Requests allowed per one-minute window for this key or session.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the current window.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the current window resets.

Unauthorized.description: No valid API key or session.

Forbidden.description: The key lacks the scope (or identity) the operation needs.

NotFound.description: No such resource in the caller’s account.

TooManyRequests.description: Over the rate limit of the key or session, or of the client address for a call without valid credentials.

details.description: The invalid fields of a 400, when the body or query failed validation.

field.description: Dotted path; empty for the whole input.

message.description: Outside NODE_ENV=production only: the internal error message.

stack.description: Outside NODE_ENV=production only: the stack trace.

retryAfter.description: Old spelling of retry_after, removed in the next release.

duration_ms.description: Null until processing has measured it.

resolution.description: Source resolution, e.g. `1920x1080`; null until processing has read it.

total.description: Every match of the filters, on all pages.

page.description: Null on a page fetched with a cursor.

status.description: The asset is gone from the API; its Sia objects are unpinned in the background.

stage.description: `upload-segments` when a finished transcode is still on disk, else `transcode`.
Pipeline step, from the latest stage-tagged log line.

retry_count.description: Retries of the pipeline stages so far: each automatic retry and each manual retry.

playback_url.description: Path of the master manifest on this deployment, e.g. `/v1/objects/<id>?type=manifest`. A path, so a client can resolve it against its own delivery base (a CDN in front of the gateway, say). It is unsigned: a private asset needs /signed or /share.

signed_url.description: Absolute url of the master manifest on PUBLIC_URL with `expires` and `sig` appended; the gateway signs the child urls in it on the fly.

poster_url.description: Absolute url of the first thumbnail, signed the same way and valid as long, so a player can show a poster for a private asset. Null when the asset has none.

signing_generation.description: The asset signing generation now in force; every older url is void.

shares.description: Map of Sia object id (hex) to a short-lived sia:// share URL the browser player resolves + downloads directly, no backend proxy.

ReconciliationRun.description: The latest run. Its shape depends on `scope`: the platform identity and operators (`deployment`) get the whole run; any other caller (`account`) gets only the drift of its own assets, because the deployment-wide counts, orphans and failure text describe other accounts and the operator’s setup. Objects the indexer pinned or unpinned within the hour before the run are work in progress and in neither list, so the in-sync count plus the orphan or missing count can be lower than the indexer or database count.

missing_ids.description: Tracked by an asset, absent from the indexer.

orphaned_ids.description: Pinned on the indexer, tracked by no asset.

status.description: `drift` when objects of the caller’s assets are missing, `failed` when the run itself could not complete.

missing_count.description: Missing objects of the caller’s assets.

already_pending.description: A run was already waiting or running, so nothing new was queued. It covers scheduled runs as well as manual ones.

stored_bytes.description: Bytes stored on Sia for these assets, before erasure coding.

error.description: Why the probe failed, when it did.

SystemStatus.description: Live status. Its shape depends on `scope`: the platform identity and operators (`deployment`) get the full report; any other caller (`account`) gets a health summary without the indexer account, the indexer url, probe error text, process uptime, the delivery cache or the deployment-wide reconciliation result.

metrics.description: The prom-client registry as JSON, one entry per metric.

id.description: The upload id: the last segment of the tus Location.

expires_at.description: Set while a rotated-out key is in its grace period.

ApiKeyCreated.description: A key as listed, plus its secret, which is only ever shown here.

secret.description: The signing secret, only ever shown here.

username.description: The provider's current username (GitHub: the login).

provider.description: The sign-in provider of this session, `local` with AUTH_DISABLED.

auth_disabled.description: True when the server runs with AUTH_DISABLED and this is the local dev account.

operator.description: Whether the account is an operator (OPERATOR_USERS) and sees deployment-wide operations data: the full system status, metrics and the whole reconciliation report. Always true for the local dev account, the one user of an AUTH_DISABLED server.

providerLabel.description: Old spelling of provider_label, removed in the next release.

authDisabled.description: Old spelling of auth_disabled, removed in the next release.

expiresAt.description: Old unix-seconds form of expires_at, removed in the next release.

SiaStorageInfo.description: Per-asset Sia storage breakdown from the indexer. Objects packed into the same slab share it; totals count each slab and sector once.

encoded_size.description: Encoded size of the slabs it references; shared slabs counted in full.

unavailable_object_ids.description: Objects the indexer could not describe on this request.

encoded_bytes.description: Bytes on hosts after erasure coding, each unique slab once.

contracts.description: Active file contracts on these hosts; null without an indexd admin API.

post.description: Creates the video asset and answers with the upload url in Location: `<PUBLIC_URL>/api/v1/uploads/<upload id>`. The upload id (a uuid) is also the id of GET and DELETE /api/v1/uploads/{id}. Send the bytes with PATCH to that url; a HEAD on it returns Upload-Metadata with videoAssetId. Metadata keys (values base64): filename, filetype (must be video/* when given), title (up to 200 characters, "Untitled" when missing), description (up to 5000 characters), accessTier or access_tier (public or private, default public). Errors answer plain text.

parameters.description: Size in bytes; at most MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE (10 GB by default).

delete.description: Without Tus-Resumable this is the REST cancel: the partial file and the asset the upload created are removed, and the session is marked cancelled (200). With Tus-Resumable it is a tus termination, which does the same and answers 204. A finished upload is the source its asset is processed and retried from and cannot be cancelled: REST answers 409, tus 400; delete the asset instead (manage scope).

get.summary: Time-limited signed playback URL.
get.description: Signs the master manifest (and the first thumbnail as a poster) for the asset. The signature covers the asset signing generation, so every url minted so far stops working when the asset tier changes or POST /api/v1/playback/{id}/signed/revoke is called. A url never lasts longer than six hours.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Asset UUID or pb_ playback ID.

parameters.name: expires_in
parameters.description: Lifetime of the url in seconds. A whole number outside 60 to 21600 is brought to the nearest bound (the answer `expires_at` says what was minted); anything else is a 400.

400.description: A malformed id, or an expires_in that is not a whole number.

409.description: The asset is not ready for playback.

post.summary: Revoke every signed URL of an asset.
post.description: Raises the asset signing generation, so every signed url minted for it so far (and every child url signed from one) is refused from now on; new ones can be minted straight away. A pb_ id revokes for its whole asset. Copies of public objects a shared cache already holds are unaffected, and sia:// share maps run until their own expiry.

parameters.description: Asset UUID or pb_ playback ID.

post.summary: Register a webhook endpoint for your account.
post.description: Events are delivered only for assets owned by the same account. Each request carries X-Sluby-Event, X-Sluby-Delivery (the same on every retry of one delivery), X-Sluby-Timestamp (Unix seconds, per attempt) and X-Sluby-Signature-V1, the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `<timestamp>.<raw body>` with the endpoint secret; receivers should refuse a timestamp more than five minutes from their clock. X-Sluby-Signature (the HMAC of the body alone) is still sent but deprecated, since it does not bind a time. The body is `{ id, event, timestamp, data }`, where `id` identifies the event across retries. The URL must be http(s) and its host must resolve only to public addresses (or to the operator's WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_NETWORKS); this is checked again before every delivery, redirects are not followed and response bodies are not read or stored. The secret is returned once.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL on a public address.

201.description: Created; includes the signing secret once.

get.summary: List webhook endpoints.
get.description: Needs `manage`, like creating them: receiver URLs often carry credentials.

post.summary: Send a signed `webhook.test` event to the endpoint now.
post.description: Delivered once, signed like any event, and recorded with the deliveries. Answers how the receiver responded: `delivered`, `status_code` (null when no response came) and `error` (why it failed, in our words).

get.summary: The endpoint's latest delivery attempts, newest first.
get.description: One entry per attempt: id, event_id, event, status_code, delivered, error, attempt (1 for the first try) and created_at. Response bodies are never stored.

Invalid input, such as a malformed id.

get.summary: Latest reconciliation run.
get.description: The platform identity and operators get the whole run, orphaned ids included; any other caller gets only the missing objects of its own assets (see ReconciliationRun). The platform identity is a key with the all-zero address, as `npm run db:seed-key` mints by default; operators are the accounts in OPERATOR_USERS, their Studio sessions and their keys.

post.description: A run scans the whole deployment, so only the platform identity or an operator may start one. It is queued unless one, manual or scheduled, is already waiting or running, so repeated calls never stack runs.

202.description: Queued, or a run was already pending.

get.summary: Library totals for the caller's account.
get.description: The platform identity gets the totals of every account. An operator gets its own, like any other account.

get.summary: Live platform status: database, redis, Sia indexer, reconciliation, cache.
get.description: The platform identity and operators get the full report; any other caller a health summary (see SystemStatus).

get.summary: Platform metrics (prometheus registry as JSON).
get.description: The registry counts the whole process, so only the platform identity or an operator may read it.

get.summary: Stream a Sia object, with byte-range support.
get.description: An object of a public asset needs nothing. An object of a private asset needs the `expires` and `sig` of a signed url (GET /api/v1/playback/{id}/signed); a manifest served that way has the urls of its children signed with the same expiry. Access follows only the asset tier: a signed playback ID gates its own /v1/stream entry, not these objects. HEAD answers the same headers without a body. A public answer carries `ETag` (the object id) and `Cache-Control: public, no-cache`, and a conditional request (`If-None-Match`) is answered 304 only after access is checked again, so a cache never keeps serving an object after its asset turns private or is deleted; the shipped nginx keeps small public objects for at most 60 seconds between checks. Objects over 8 MB are streamed and never cached.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: Expiry (unix seconds) of a signed url. Required for a private object.

parameters.name: sig
parameters.description: Signature of a signed url. Required for a private object.

304.description: Still public and unchanged (a conditional request).

400.description: Not a Sia object id (64 lowercase hex characters).

403.description: A private object without a valid, unexpired signature of the asset current signing generation; `reason` says why.

404.description: No asset holds the object, its asset is being deleted, or the indexer no longer has it.

502.description: The Sia network did not answer; try again.

503.description: The database did not answer; try again.

get.summary: Master HLS manifest for an asset or playback ID.
get.description: A private asset or a signed-policy playback ID needs the `expires` and `sig` of the asset’s signed master url; the child urls in the answer are then signed too. A signed playback ID gates only this entry: on a public asset its objects stay public, so the bytes are not private (make the asset private for that), and other embeds of the asset keep playing. A public answer is cached like a public object.

parameters.name: videoAssetId
parameters.description: Asset UUID or pb_ playback ID.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: Expiry (unix seconds) from the signed master URL. Required when gated.

parameters.name: sig
parameters.description: Signature from the signed master URL. Required when gated.

304.description: Still public and unchanged (a conditional request).

403.description: Gated, and no valid, unexpired signature; `reason` says why.

404.description: No such asset or playback ID, or the asset is not ready.

502.description: The Sia network did not answer; try again.

503.description: The database did not answer; try again.

get.summary: Per-object sia:// share URLs for direct-from-Sia playback, without credentials.
get.description: Gated like /v1/stream: a public asset by its id or a public playback ID needs nothing. A private asset or a signed-policy playback ID needs the `expires` and `sig` of its signed master URL, and the shares then never outlive `expires`. Expiries are capped like the authenticated route (six hours, one hour when gated) and rounded to five-minute slots that the server caches, so repeated calls do not mint again. A gated map is sent `private, no-store`; a public one may be kept by the shipped nginx for up to a minute and is revalidated by every other cache. Share URLs already handed out keep working until they expire, whatever happens to the asset meanwhile.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Asset UUID or pb_ playback ID.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: Expiry (unix seconds) from the signed master URL. Required when gated.

parameters.name: sig
parameters.description: Signature from the signed master URL. Required when gated.

503.description: The database did not answer; try again.

get.summary: Delivery cache statistics.
